message.content:
Yes, the original Coca-Cola formula did contain cocaine. Here's what the historical records show:

## The Original Formula

When Dr. John Stith Pemberton invented Coca-Cola in 1886, the drink contained extract from coca leaves, which naturally contained trace amounts of cocaine. At the time, cocaine was legal and commonly used in patent medicines and tonics. Pemberton, a pharmacist and Civil War veteran who had developed a morphine addiction from war injuries, was inspired by "coca wines" like Vin Mariani and believed in the medicinal properties of coca leaves.

The name "Coca-Cola" itself derives from two of its original key ingredients:
- **Coca** - from coca leaves (containing cocaine)
- **Cola** - from kola nuts (containing caffeine)

## When It Was Removed

The cocaine was removed from the formula in **1903** (some sources cite 1901 or 1904 as the exact timing). The Coca-Cola Company switched to using "spent" or de-cocainized coca leaves, which maintained the flavor profile without the active drug.

The removal was driven by several factors:
- Shifting public attitudes and growing awareness of cocaine's addictive properties
- Increasing regulation (the Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906)
- Racial prejudices of the era, as cocaine became associated with Black communities in the South

## Today's Coca-Cola

Modern Coca-Cola still uses coca leaves for flavoring, but only after the cocaine has been extracted. The de-cocainized leaves are supplied to Coca-Cola under strict DEA supervision. The extracted cocaine is used for medical and research purposes.

3. https://www.thetakeout.com/1788713/why-coca-cola-had-cocaine/
4. https://thetraininggyms.com/blog/coca-cola-is-worse-than-cocaine/
